triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The 9903.05.86 annex carve-out predicate was gated from 2026-07-23, a day before the forced-labor 301 action applies (FR 2026-15181 DATES: entries on or after 12:01 a.m. July 24, 2026), so the heading's carve-out was live a day early relative to the action it belongs to.
triage.triage_notes: Single-rule module; only the effective_from changed, formula article_provided_for_in_subdivision_b_of_us_note_52 untouched. Source verified: us/rulemaking/federal-register/2026-07-28/2026-15181 DATES reads 'The additional rates of duty are applicable with respect to products that are entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 24, 2026'. Note the sibling module forced-labor-presidential-action.yaml (the memorandum of July 23, 2026, rate parameters) keeps effective_from 2026-07-23 and was deliberately not changed, which is consistent: the memorandum date differs from the entry-date gate. Companion test unchanged.
triage.verifier_justification: The only change in this module is the single version window start, `effective_from: '2026-07-23'` → `'2026-07-24'`, which is a meaning-bearing field (version window / effective date), so it cannot be mechanical, and no formula, parameter, scope, or logic moved, so no other kind fits. I resolved the governing source through the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union): FR 2026-15181 DATES reads "The additional rates of duty are applicable with respect to products that are entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 24, 2026", and Annex I.A — the block that inserts the new subchapter III provisions effective July 24, 2026 — is where heading 9903.05.86 and U.S. note 52(b) appear, so the heading simply did not operate on 2026-07-23. The pre-fix date was therefore wrong against the source rather than an enhancement or a policy choice; the PR body had itself flagged the inconsistency ("although heading modules carry effective_from 2026-07-23") and the repair commit corrects it in the same direction across the whole forced-labor 301 family, while moving Brazil 9903.05.01 the other way to 07-22 per FR 2026-14542 — a pattern consistent with per-notice DATES alignment, not a blanket shift.
triage.verifier_notes: Refutation attempts that failed: (1) mechanical — excluded, effective dates are explicitly meaning-bearing and nothing else in the file changed; (2) boundary_direction — the fix moves the date value, not the strictness/inclusivity of a comparison (effective_from stays an inclusive start), so wrong_period_or_effective_date is the precise kind; (3) not_a_defect — the source settles it, the heading is created by Annex I.A effective 2026-07-24. Two caveats a reviewer should see. First, the module's own `corpus_citation_path` (us/statute/hts/9903.05.86) resolves to article-description and rate text with no date at all; the date authority is FR 2026-15181, which this module does not cite (the composition does, carrying the DATES excerpt as a proof atom at us/rulemaking/federal-register/2026-07-28/2026-15181). So the disagreement is with the governing notice named in the commit message, not with text under the module's own citation path. Second, 9903.05.86 is a carve-out the duty headings except out of, and those headings also started 07-24, so the one-day-early window likely had no standalone computed effect — still an encoded-meaning defect, not merely cosmetic. Unrelated nuance visible in the same FR, out of scope here: Annex I.B modifies the article description of 9903.05.90 effective 2026-07-31, while module 007 (forced-labor-metals-9903-05-90) carries a single version from 2026-07-24; that module may warrant its own look.
